dedupe_keys.name: houston hurricane beryl 2024 power outage disables stormwater pump and leaves intersection flooded houston public media

description: This news case documents how a power outage after Hurricane Beryl, a Category 1 storm that left more than 2.26 million CenterPoint Energy customers without power in July 2024, kept a Houston underpass flooded. Eight days after landfall more than a foot of stagnant water still covered the Elgin Street and Lockwood Drive intersection near the University of Houston, because Houston Public Works said its stormwater pumps require power and the pump along the Gulf Freeway had none. Barricades stood from 8 July, police patrolled in shifts, and METRO bus routes 4, 25 and 80 detoured, adding up to 30 minutes. Public works reported no recent 311 drainage requests at the site. Coverage: a single pump station and intersection. Access: a free news article; the licence is not stated. Caveats: journalism with limited technical detail on pump capacity or restoration time. It illustrates power to drainage dependency for cascading failure and resilience models, and relates to the New Orleans drainage root cause analysis in the catalogue.
